threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think Hackney is just hipster cafes and galleries. Real locals know the best pie and mash spot isn’t in the guidebook.
Caught a guy on the 333 last night, serenading the late-night crowd with an old Whitney track. Only in Brixton would that vibe feel totally normal.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a cat confidently strolling down Weserstraße while a group of hipsters debated the best falafel in town. Only in Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain will you find spontaneous techno raves under the S-Bahn tracks, with the echoes of trains adding to the bass.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know a local by how they navigate the BART delays. It's all about that sidestep to avoid the oncoming stampede on Mission St when Civic Center shuts down.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Watched a tourist try to pay with a Starbucks gift card instead of a Clipper at the Muni stop. The confusion was real, classic SF moment.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all locals love paella. In Gràcia, you’re more likely to find folks raving about calçots and a good xató, especially in winter.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They’re the ones still looking up at the street signs, fumbling with the map while everyone else zigzags past like it’s second nature.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You stand at the bus stop, staring at the timetable app instead of just looking up to see the bus actually coming down the road.
Caught the 68 last night; the driver was giving a Shakespearean monologue between stops. Only in Brixton do you get drama with your late-night ride.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I realized I was truly home when I heard a street musician playing a lullaby on a theremin at Herrfurthplatz, and kids were dancing like it was a block party.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a late-night currywurst stall serving vegan options and a techno DJ spinning records at 3 AM in the adjacent park.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by how they improvise when BART breaks down—like making plans on the fly or just ordering an Uber while laughing it off.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus today that was so packed, I swear I saw someone juggling to entertain the crowd. Only in San Francisco, right?

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists assume all bars serve tapas, but many only do platillos. You won’t find patatas bravas everywhere; look closer, locals have their favorites.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by how they still ask for pa amb tomaquet in English, expecting the waiter to understand. It’s the little things.
